dimensions.name: Contract & semantics reverse-engineering

evidence.note: Systematically reads helpers.py, run.sh, and every dev_test file plus oracle_fixtures before writing any server code — comprehensive mapping of the exact endpoint/payload/discriminator contract the client exercises.
Deliberate library selection: probes installed packages then chooses Flask+Flask-Sock+openpyxl with explicit rationale for HTTP+WS+XLSX needs.

Probes genuinely tricky Excel semantics as subsystems are reached — #CIRC!/self-cycle, LET/LAMBDA application, spill recovery/shrink/C1# syntax, date-format mm minutes-vs-months, HEX2DEC negatives, iterative fixed-point, INDEX row-0 — rather than assuming.

Verifies openpyxl actually supports required xlsx round-trip features (cached values via XML injection, conditional formatting, named ranges, data validation), re-consulting the library capability per new subsystem.

Reads only one oracle fixture (aggregates.json); does not systematically reconcile against the held-out LibreOffice ground-truth corpus, and builds no durable contract-map artifact — keeping this below the level-10 anchor.

dimensions.reasoning: The agent exhaustively read helpers.py, run.sh, and all smoke tests to extract concrete wire shapes, chose libraries deliberately, verified openpyxl feature support, and repeatedly probed Excel semantics for the hard areas (spill, #CIRC!, iterative calc, date formats, xlsx round-trip) as it reached each subsystem — squarely matching the level-8 anchor and extending toward 10's 'contract-driven throughout.' It stops short of 10 because it grounds semantics in its own Excel knowledge rather than systematically reconciling against the LibreOffice oracle corpus, and produces no durable cross-referenced contract map.

dimensions.name: Sequencing the feature surface into checkable milestones

evidence.note: Front-loaded exploration of all dev tests/helpers/libs, then laid out an explicit dependency-ordered module decomposition (refs → parser → engine → funcs → workbook → server → xlsx) — sequencing by what depends on what.

Got a live server + health + persistence + contract-correct core green (dev tests as done-checks) BEFORE pushing breadth, then prioritized the load-bearing graph/recompute/cycle-detection correctness to reach 131/131 — matches the 8 anchor's 'core round-trip green before breadth'.

Performance (a highest-risk load-bearing requirement) was validated only after breadth work started; found 100k import at ~200s, then profiled and fixed O(N^2). Load-bearing perf layer was checked reactively rather than front-loaded — keeps it below the 10 anchor.

After base green, repeatedly re-enumerated hidden-suite risk lists and iterated, re-running the dev suite as a regression checkpoint after nearly every change — a living but flat running to-do, not an explicitly re-ordered milestone hierarchy with articulated per-item done-criteria.

dimensions.reasoning: The agent solidly phased the enormous surface by dependency (parser/engine before graph before analyst/xlsx breadth) and used the runnable dev suite as a concrete done-check at each transition, getting live-server/persistence/contract core green before breadth — squarely the behavior the 8 anchor describes. It falls short of 10 because the decomposition was expressed as a module list plus recurring flat risk enumeration rather than an explicit, re-ordered milestone hierarchy with pre-stated done-criteria, and the highest-risk performance layer was validated reactively mid-stream rather than front-loaded. That places it just above the well-checkpointed-phasing level, at a 7.

dimensions.name: Self-built verification beyond the smoke suite

evidence.note: Built performance probes against the stated ceilings; found 100k import at 197s (over 30s limit), diagnosed O(N^2) hotspot, and fixed to ~1s — verification driving fixes.
Self-authored xlsx round-trip tests via openpyxl: data_only cached values, named ranges, conditional-format and data-validation export/import round-trips, iterating on failures.
Hand-checked format strings against expected Excel renderings, caught the h:mm minutes-vs-months bug, and fixed it.
Targeted probes for spill dependents, shrinking, recovery, INDEX spill and the C1# spill-range syntax — subsystem checks beyond the smoke suite.
Ran dev_tests/run.sh regularly after every change, but treated it as a regression guard alongside its own richer checks, not the sole signal.
For collaboration, reasoned that WS tests suffice rather than constructing seq/broadcast probes — a gap that keeps it below the level-10 systematic/oracle-grounded harness.

dimensions.reasoning: The agent ran the smoke suite regularly (well above level 3-5) but crucially constructed its own targeted verification well beyond it: performance benchmarks against the spec's ceilings, xlsx round-trips via openpyxl, error-sentinel and spill-collision probes, and function/format spot-checks against Excel-known values — repeatedly using failures to drive fixes, which is the defining behavior of level 8. It stops short of 10 because the checks were ad-hoc scripts rather than a systematic harness, expected values came from the agent's own Excel knowledge rather than a LibreOffice oracle, and some subsystems (collab, goal-seek) were reasoned about instead of probed.

dimensions.name: Tracking done-vs-remaining across a huge surface

evidence.note: Iterative debugging of chain recompute and cycle detection, with precise reconciliation against the dev suite ('76 passing', then '129/131 passing! Two failures:' naming each). Tracks done-vs-remaining against verification results, not just self-report.

Detects a stalled subsystem: notices the 100k import hanging, diagnoses quadratic behavior, localizes the O(N^2) hotspot in transitive_dependents_with_cycles, fixes it (197s->1s), and re-verifies. Detection of a stuck state with deliberate effort reallocation, no looping.

Recurring enumerated lists of outstanding hidden-suite areas (CF export, DV export, pivot cols, spill # syntax, XLSX cached values), addressed one-by-one with a full-suite re-run after each. Shows rolling tracking of remaining surface, though re-derived each time rather than a single maintained ledger.

Catches that funcs.py wasn't imported by workbook.py and correctly reasons why tests still passed (server imports it), rather than looping in confusion — accurate state tracking of a subtle wiring issue.

The ~150-function catalog is built in a single systematic burst by category (math/stats/text/logical/lookup/date/dynamic-array/financial/etc.) but never subsequently checked off in a done/partial/not-started ledger; later coverage is spot-checked ad hoc — the main gap below the level-8 anchor.

dimensions.reasoning: The agent maintains granular, continuously verification-reconciled awareness of done-vs-remaining (exact pass counts after nearly every change) and demonstrably detects a stalled performance subsystem, diagnosing and fixing it without circular thrashing — clearly beyond the 'simple checklist' of anchor 5. It falls short of anchor 8's 'live, granular ledger of the function catalog and endpoint families' because tracking is prose-based and re-derived (recurring brainstorm lists) rather than a sustained single-source ledger, and the large function catalog is built once and only spot-checked. This places it at a 7, between the 5 and 8 anchors.

dimensions.name: Course-correcting on falsified Excel/perf assumptions

evidence.note: Discovered single-batch recompute violated topological order; diagnosed the dependency-graph assumption and reworked patch_cells to recompute all reachable formula nodes in topo order rather than local patching.

Recursion on cycles falsified the naive eval model; added Kahn's cycle detection, then caught two further wrong assumptions (self-loops excluded by p!=x; LAMBDA-via-LET call resolution) and reworked each root cause.

100k import at 197s falsified the perf assumption; profiled to the exact O(N^2) line in transitive_dependents, rewrote to O(N), re-measured 197s->1.08s — deliberate root-cause perf correction with re-verification.
XLSX data_only returned None; diagnosed openpyxl writes empty <v/>, adjusted the post-processing approach to fill cached values, then re-ran full suite.
Date-format 'mm' rendered as month after 'h:'; recognized the Excel minutes-vs-months context rule and fixed the underlying handler.
Re-ran the full smoke suite after nearly every change, confirming corrections didn't regress unaffected subsystems — the re-verify loop of the top anchors.

dimensions.reasoning: The agent repeatedly detected divergence from verification signals (failing tests, perf measurements, function probes), diagnosed the root assumption (topological recompute, cycle model, quadratic graph traversal, xlsx caching, date-format semantics), and reworked the affected design rather than piling on patches, re-verifying via the full suite each time — matching the level-8 rework behavior and much of the level-10 'diagnose-revise-reverify without derailing' pattern. It falls just short of a clean 10 because a couple of fixes (e.g. the step-67 monkey-patch) were workarounds and some corrections were reactive to surfaced failures rather than detected early.

dimensions.name: Coverage allocation under finite effort

evidence.note: Up front reads every dev test/helper, names the task a 'massive undertaking' and commits to 'build this efficiently' — framing effort allocation against the full graded surface rather than diving into one corner.

Builds the entire function catalog breadth-first (math, stats, distributions, financial, date, engineering, database, lookup, text, dynamic arrays) and all endpoint families before any deep edge-case work — securing broad working coverage first.

Explicitly reasons about the hidden suite: 'the verifier has more comprehensive grading. Let me look at corner cases I might have missed', 'Hidden tests on text functions - my modern text functions are basic', and defers items judged 'probably not tested' (sheet rename with cross-sheet refs) — conscious return-weighted triage.

Consciously declines to invest in REST->WS broadcast after reasoning 'all tests use WebSocket directly, not REST. So my current setup is OK' — deliberately NOT over-investing in a likely-ungraded path.

Latter half is a stream of targeted depth probes on high-risk areas (spill shrink/# syntax, iterative calc cycles, date-format mm context, 1000-cell perf), each checked against likelihood of being graded — depth timeboxed to plausibly high-yield spots.

dimensions.reasoning: The agent clearly matches the level-8 anchor: it explicitly reasons about graded return, secures broad working coverage across the entire function catalog and endpoint families before deep edge-case work, and consciously defers low-yield niches ('probably not tested', REST->WS 'OK'). It shows some level-10 traits (risk-based depth probing, weighing marginal coverage) but the allocation is a stream of ad-hoc 'let me also check' probes rather than a deliberate, revisited allocation ledger with explicit reallocation, so it falls short of 10.

rubric.task_read: This is an extremely long-horizon, high-complexity build: a full Excel-clone product (persistent HTTP server + SPA + WebSocket collab) with a formula engine spanning ~150 functions, Excel-365 dynamic arrays/spill, a dependency graph with performance-bounded dirty recompute, xlsx/CSV round-trip, and a large analyst surface (defined names, formats, conditional formatting, pivots, locale, validation, goal seek, iterative calc). The exact wire contract is under-specified and must be reverse-engineered from an existing Python client, and grading is on a much larger HIDDEN suite plus value-by-value comparison against a LibreOffice oracle. This task demands maximal, sustained meta-work across all five faculties: deep upfront orientation on the contract, aggressive decomposition/sequencing of an enormous surface, self-built verification well beyond the smoke suite, tight progress tracking, and constant course-correction as Excel edge cases falsify assumptions.

dimensions.name: Contract & semantics reverse-engineering
dimensions.description: Extracting the exact wire shapes from /dev_tests/helpers.py and the smoke suite, and grounding formula/feature behavior in Excel/LibreOffice semantics, before and while building.
dimensions.why_it_matters: The wire shapes are defined ONLY by what the first-party client calls, and grading compares values against a LibreOffice oracle. Guessing shapes or semantics guarantees hidden-suite failures no matter how good the code is; this is the single highest-leverage meta-activity here.

anchors.0: Starts writing the server/engine without reading helpers.py or dev_tests; invents endpoint and cell shapes from imagination.
anchors.3: Skims helpers.py once; picks up a few obvious shapes but leaves most of the contract (patch/fill/sort/spill/collab payloads, kind discriminator, envelope) inferred loosely.
anchors.5: Reads helpers.py and run.sh to extract the concrete request/response shapes it exercises, chooses libraries (OOXML I/O, formula eval) deliberately, and forms a working model of the core cell/formula contract.
anchors.8: Systematically maps every endpoint, discriminator, and payload the client touches into an explicit reference; probes Excel semantics for genuinely tricky areas (spill ghosts, #SPILL!/#CIRC!, iterative fixed-point, locale canonicalization, xlsx openpyxl round-trip) rather than assuming; verifies chosen libraries actually support required features (CF, styles, named ranges).
anchors.10: Builds a durable, cross-referenced contract map reconciling helpers.py, the smoke suite, and Excel/LibreOffice ground truth; proactively surfaces ambiguities and resolves them from observed client behavior; re-consults the client/oracle as new subsystems are reached, so implementation is contract-driven throughout rather than only at the start.

dimensions.name: Sequencing the feature surface into checkable milestones
dimensions.description: Breaking an enormous, interdependent surface into an ordered hierarchy of sub-goals — each with an explicit done-check — sequenced by dependency and risk.
dimensions.why_it_matters: There are dozens of endpoint families and ~150 functions with hard dependencies (health/persistence → contract → engine → graph → dynamic arrays → analyst surface → collab/xlsx). Without deliberate ordering and done-criteria, the agent cannot sustain progress or know when a layer is solid enough to build on.

anchors.0: Treats the whole product as one undifferentiated push; jumps between unrelated features with no ordering or completion criteria.
anchors.3: A flat, one-time to-do list of features with no dependency ordering and no per-item way to know it's done.
anchors.5: Phases the work into sensible stages (skeleton/health first, then engine, then extras) with rough checkpoints per stage.
anchors.8: An explicit milestone hierarchy sequenced by dependency and risk (get a live server + persistence + contract-correct core cell round-trip green before breadth), each milestone with a concrete done-check tied to a runnable test.
anchors.10: A living, dependency-aware milestone plan that front-loads the highest-risk load-bearing layers (dependency graph, spill, recompute correctness/performance), defines done-criteria in terms of verifiable behavior, and is revisited and re-ordered as scope understanding deepens — never a static checklist.

dimensions.name: Self-built verification beyond the smoke suite
dimensions.description: Deliberately constructing checks — formula-value oracles, round-trip tests, error-sentinel and performance probes — rather than trusting the non-exhaustive smoke suite.
dimensions.why_it_matters: The spec explicitly warns the visible suite is non-exhaustive and grading is a much larger hidden suite plus cell-by-cell comparison to LibreOffice. An agent that only runs run.sh is flying blind on the majority of what's graded.

anchors.0: No verification; assumes code works, or never runs the provided smoke suite.
anchors.3: Runs dev_tests/run.sh occasionally and treats a green smoke run as done.
anchors.5: Runs the smoke suite regularly and hand-checks a few formulas/endpoints against expected Excel values.
anchors.8: Builds its own targeted tests well beyond the smoke suite — spot-checking function outputs against known Excel results, exercising error sentinels, spill collisions, xlsx round-trip via openpyxl, and the stated performance bounds — using failures to drive fixes.
anchors.10: Stands up a systematic verification harness covering breadth of the catalog and subsystems (dynamic arrays, collab seq/broadcast, locale, iterative calc, goal-seek convergence, xlsx fidelity), grounds expected values in an Excel/LibreOffice oracle, benchmarks the performance ceilings, and treats verification as the primary signal steering what to build/fix next.

dimensions.name: Tracking done-vs-remaining across a huge surface
dimensions.description: Maintaining an accurate live picture of which functions, endpoints, and subsystems are complete vs outstanding, and detecting stuck/circular states.
dimensions.why_it_matters: With ~150 functions and ~15 feature families over a very long horizon, it is easy to lose the plot, double-implement, or silently drop whole categories; sustained accurate tracking is what prevents both gaps and thrash.

anchors.0: No sense of what's done or left; forgets whole feature areas or repeatedly reworks the same thing without noticing.
anchors.3: Vague mental tracking; periodically rediscovers unfinished areas by accident.
anchors.5: Keeps a checklist of major features and updates it as areas are completed.
anchors.8: Maintains a live, granular ledger of the function catalog and endpoint families (done / partial / not-started), and notices when it is stuck or re-debugging the same issue, adjusting rather than looping.
anchors.10: Sustains an accurate running picture across the entire surface for the whole horizon, reconciled against verification results (not just self-report), promptly detects thrashing/circular debugging or a stalled subsystem, and reallocates effort deliberately in response.

dimensions.name: Course-correcting on falsified Excel/perf assumptions
dimensions.description: Revising design or approach when reality — Excel edge cases, spill/recompute behavior, performance limits, contract mismatches — diverges from expectations.
dimensions.why_it_matters: Excel semantics and the dependency/spill/iterative machinery are riddled with edge cases; initial designs (e.g. naive recompute, spill handling, locale parsing) will be falsified. Barrelling ahead on a wrong assumption compounds into wide test failures.

anchors.0: Ignores contradicting evidence; keeps pushing a falsified design (e.g. recompute that misses dependents or blows the perf budget) unchanged.
anchors.3: Reacts only to hard crashes with local patches; doesn't revisit the underlying approach when results are subtly wrong.
anchors.5: Fixes issues as tests surface them and makes reasonable local design changes when something clearly doesn't work.
anchors.8: Recognizes when a failure signals a wrong assumption (dependency-graph model, spill materialization, topological order, contract shape) and reworks the relevant design rather than piling on patches.
anchors.10: Detects divergence early from verification signals, diagnoses the root assumption, revises the affected design deliberately, and re-verifies — repeatedly steering the build back on course without derailing unaffected subsystems.

dimensions.name: Coverage allocation under finite effort
dimensions.description: Deciding which of the vast feature/function set to build (and in what breadth-vs-depth balance) to maximize graded coverage on the hidden suite given limited time.
dimensions.why_it_matters: The surface is far larger than can be perfected; graded return is maximized by consciously trading breadth of working features against depth on a few. This allocation decision is distinct from ordering milestones — it's about what NOT to over-invest in and where partial coverage still scores.

anchors.0: No triage: rabbit-holes on one function/feature (e.g. perfecting one distribution) while leaving whole graded areas unimplemented.
anchors.3: Implements in arbitrary order with no regard to graded return; over-polishes some corners while omitting entire common families.
anchors.5: Roughly prioritizes high-frequency, high-value features (core math/lookup/text, cell round-trip) before niche ones.
anchors.8: Explicitly reasons about graded return — securing broad working coverage of common functions and endpoints before deep edge-case work, and consciously deferring or timeboxing low-yield niches.
anchors.10: Runs a deliberate, revisited allocation strategy: breadth-first correctness across the catalog and endpoint families, timeboxed depth on high-risk/high-value areas, and reallocation as verification reveals where marginal effort buys the most hidden-suite coverage.
